classification.difficultyReason: Read bar frequencies, select categories for a percentage, and distinguish counting families from counting children by weighting each category by its frequency.

content.prompt: The column graph below shows the number of children in families that completed a survey.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3, graph between the shared stem and part a
spec.description: Separated columns for 0–4 children, with horizontal gridlines at every labelled frequency. Source teal columns are represented by the standard blue graph palette.
spec.answerVisibility: All graph data are permanent student-visible givens.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many of the families have more than two children?

answer.worked:
Families with more than two children have three or four children.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number of families}&=8+2\\\text{Number of families}&=10\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What percentage of the families have no child or one child, correct to the nearest 1%?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Number with zero or one child}&=8+16\\\text{Number with zero or one child}&=24\\\text{Percentage}&=\frac{24}{44}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage}&\approx55\%\quad\text{(nearest 1\%)}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: In total, how many children are there?

answer.worked:
Multiply each number of children by its frequency, then add.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total children}&=0\times8+1\times16+2\times10+3\times8+4\times2\\\text{Total children}&=0+16+20+24+8\\\text{Total children}&=68\end{align*}$$
